transcript:
Meeting: Redwood Console - Tracing & Request Logs Debugging Demo
Recorded: 2026-12-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Nebula - Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Nebula - SRE), Ava Thompson (Nebula - Product)

Summary: Quick walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing and request logs for debugging LLM request failures and latency spikes. Showed error-analysis view, request-level logs, span-level traces, and filtering/redaction options. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs and security (SOC2, KMS). Agreed to POC data exchange and pricing follow-up.

Topics: tracing overview, error analysis, request logs, KV cache visibility, canary rollouts, VPC/KMS concerns, debugging flows for inference timeouts and mismatched outputs

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, and with me is Liam, our SE. Quick sound check?
[00:18] Maya (Nebula): Sounds good, thanks, we're excited to see the tracing view, we've been hitting intermittent 500s and some tail latency on our re-ranking route.
[00:29] Liam (Redwood SE): Cool, we'll jump straight in. I'll share the console - apologies if the deck link is slightly different, I also dropped a short demo recording: https://redwood.ai/decks/trace-demo
[00:42] Liam: So top left is the tracing pane, this is end-to-end request traces. Each row is a request, and the flame view expands into spans. You can correlate with request logs down here.
[01:03] Carlos (Nebula): Quick question, can we see KV cache hits in the trace? Our re-ranker uses a prefix cache and sometimes misses cause slowdowns.
[01:12] Liam: Yes, we surfice - sorry, surface KV cache span types, you can filter for cache.fetch and cache.hit. Sometimes auto-transcriber messes with "KV" as "K V" but it's there.
[01:26] Maya: Great. Also we need to redact cardholder data, so any shared logs must be redacted before you look.
[01:33] Sofia: Totally, we have redaction built-in in the request logs export and we support field-level redaction. We'll send our redaction checklist with the SOC2 docs.
[02:05] Liam: Demoing an error case: here we have a 504 from the Dedicated pool. You can see the trace shows a long decode span and then a timeout at the runtime. I can click into the span to see metrics and the stack: model version, sequence length, GPU ID, and kernel timings.
[02:33] Ava (Nebula): That GPU ID is helpful. We had noisy neighbors on one node last week, but aren't on dedicated yet.
[02:42] Liam: Right, for Hosted customers we do smart routing by policy, you can route by latency SLO or cost. For Dedicated, if you pin a model version we still include per-route traces for visibility but isolation is stronger.
[03:10] Maya: Do you keep request bodies in logs? We have strict retention rules.
[03:18] Sofia: By default request logs include request ID and truncated prompt, but full bodies are only stored if you enable verbose logging for the POC; we support encrypted storage with your KMS for Private deployments. We'll include the data residency section in the docs.
[03:45] Carlos: How long are traces kept? Our compliance requires 90 days of audit logs.
[03:51] Liam: Console supports configurable retention – short term hot traces (30 days) with long-term archival to your S3 for up to 365 days on enterprise plans. Policy and retention options are in the security pack.
[04:12] Sofia: We should share the SOC2 and ISO attestation plus our audit log schema after this call.
[04:20] Maya: Thanks. Can we walk through a real debugging flow? E.g., a request that returns hallucinated entities vs. a failure?
[04:30] Liam: Yep, here is a request where user saw inconsistent entity extraction. In the trace, you can inspect prompt tokens, top-k sampling params and model variant. See that at span decode we switched to a quantized variant which changed sampling temperature, causing output drift.
[04:58] Maya: Is that an automatic fallback? We saw a fallback to "rq-quant" last week.
[05:05] Liam: Yes, smart routing can fallback to quantized variants when capacity is constrained. We expose the fallback reason in the trace metadata: capacity, region, or cost-driven. You can also set policy to disallow fallback for critical routes.
[05:30] Carlos: For the POC we'll want deterministic behavior, so disallow fallback and pin model version. How do rollouts look in console?
[05:38] Liam: Rollouts are here - you can set canary percentage, automatic rollback on quality regression (we tie into Redwood Optimize evals), or manual. Traces during rollouts are grouped so you can compare latency/quality side-by-side.
[06:02] Ava: Nice. Can you search request logs for error patterns? Like all requests that had decode > 200ms and 500 status?
[06:10] Liam: Absolutely, the request log query supports boolean filters and histogram buckets. Example query saved: status:500 AND decode_ms:>200. You can also pin a query as an alert source.
[06:30] Maya: What's the typical overhead of tracing? We worry about extra latency.
[06:36] Sofia: Tracing is asynchronous and sampling-based by default; full tracing can add negligible overhead. For POC we usually enable full traces for a small percentage of traffic.
[06:52] Carlos: We need information on encryption at rest and key management.
[06:57] Sofia: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments and Dedicated as an add-on. Will attach KMS integration guide.
[07:20] Liam: Switching to request logs view - here's a raw request log entry. Note fields: request_id, route, model_id, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, decode_ms, parent_span_id, sampler_flag. Some transcription will show "decode mouse" instead of decode_ms, ignore that.
[07:50] Maya: Can you export logs in redacted form to our S3?
[07:54] Liam: Yes, export to customer S3 with field-level redaction rules applied. We support event streaming to your SIEM as well.
[08:10] Ava: About latency spikes: sometimes we see a cluster of 429s during peak - can tracing show throttling cause?
[08:18] Liam: Throttling shows as a specific span and there's a reason code in the trace: RATE_LIMIT or POOL_EXHAUST. You can correlate with capacity metrics to see if autoscaling didn't keep up.
[08:38] Maya: Do you offer synthetic load testing tools?
[08:42] Sofia: We have a benchmark harness and suggested workloads; Liam will share a sample CSV with request distributions.
[08:55] Liam: Sharing link to sample benchmarks: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/nebulafinance.csv
[09:05] Carlos: For the Dedicated quote, can we get a 4-GPU pool with burst to Hosted if needed?
[09:12] Sofia: Yes, Dedicated supports burst to Hosted and we can model cost for expected QPS. We'll include pricing in follow-up.
[09:24] Maya: One more technical: can we see per-span GPU kernel timings? Our infra team wants to see top kernels that dominate the decode.
[09:33] Liam: Yes kernel-level timings are available; they're surfaced under the decode span as micro-metrics. For quantized runs you can see reduced memory and different kernel shapes.
[10:00] Ava: Any limitations for on-prem?
[10:04] Liam: On-prem package supports most runtime features but some managed telemetry is replaced with local collectors; we ship an agent for traces which forwards metadata to your control plane.
[10:18] Maya: Okay good. Can you show a live debug of a 500?
[10:22] Liam: Sure, filtering for status:500. Here's a request — trace shows decode spike at 1.2s, then a mem alloc error in the runtime logs. The request log has a stack snippet: "oom_alloc at gpu.cu:234".
[10:45] Carlos: That's consistent with the node we identified. Could be batch sizing issue.
[10:50] Liam: We also include batch-size histograms. See these spans where batch size jumps to 64 and decode_ms increases. You can set intelligent batching recommendations in Optimize to limit batch growth for low-latency routes.
[11:12] Maya: That's interesting. Can Optimize run rules to cap batch size for particular route names?
[11:17] Liam: Yes, Optimize suggestions can be applied per-route, and you can auto-enforce them if you want.
[11:35] Sofia: Quick pause for clarifying next steps. We'll send SOC2/ISO, KMS guide, and the Dedicated quote. Liam to share the traces dump and benchmarks.
[11:50] Ava: For timelines - we'd like to start a 2-week POC mid-December.
[11:55] Sofia: We can do 2026-12-15 for POC kickoff, I'll pencil it in and send calendar invite.
[12:05] Carlos: One more question on RBAC - can we restrict who at Nebula can view raw prompts?
[12:10] Liam: Yes RBAC supports role-based access; field-level permissions can hide prompt bodies from non-privileged roles.
[12:28] Maya: Last thing - competitors, we've looked at Anthropic and Bedrock for routing features. How do you compare on observability?
[12:36] Sofia: Our distinguishing piece is integrated trace->request log correlation and rollout-linked quality evals. We expose per-route cost/latency so product teams can make tradeoffs.
[12:50] Ava: OK that helps.
[12:58] Liam: Wrapping up here's the recap: 1) Redwood will provide SOC2, KMS guide, and pricing for Dedicated with burst; 2) We'll share benchmark CSV and a traces export; 3) POC kickoff 2026-12-15; 4) Action items in follow-up email.
[13:20] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and the invite.
[13:28] Maya: Thanks, good session.

References shared: https://redwood.ai/decks/trace-demo, https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/nebulafinance.csv
